title: Running an Election in the Heart of Election Denialism

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 你好，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for DealBook, a daily newsletter at the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我为《纽约时报》的每日通讯 DealBook 报道商业和政策新闻。

sentences.en: On November 18th, I'm going to be interviewing some of the most consequential leaders in business, politics, and culture, including J.D.
sentences.zh: 11月18日，我将在纽约市举行的 DealBook 峰会上现场采访一些商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的人物，包括 J.D.

sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜·拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及其他许多人。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: This is a daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: Half the Republican candidates on the ballot in November's election still deny that President Biden won the 2020 election.
sentences.zh: 11月选举中，半数共和党候选人仍然否认拜登总统赢得了2020年大选。

sentences.en: A level of denialism that is fueling an unprecedented volume of harassment and threats toward election workers.
sentences.zh: 这种程度的否认主义正在助长针对选举工作人员前所未有的骚扰和威胁。

sentences.en: Few have experienced those attacks as viscerally as election workers in Arizona, a state that Donald Trump still refuses to acknowledge he lost,
sentences.zh: 很少有人像亚利桑那州的选举工作人员那样深刻地感受到这些攻击，在这个唐纳德·特朗普至今拒绝承认失败的州，

sentences.en: and where the Republican candidates for governor, attorney general, and secretary of state all embrace his false claim that the election was stolen.
sentences.zh: 而且那里的共和党州长、总检察长和州务卿候选人都支持他关于选举被窃取的虚假主张。

sentences.en: Today, a conversation with the top election official in Arizona's biggest county
sentences.zh: 今天，我们与亚利桑那州最大县的最高选举官员进行了一次对话，

sentences.en: about what it's like to oversee voting when so many of the voters themselves doubt the legitimacy of the process.
sentences.zh: 谈谈当如此多的选民本身都怀疑选举过程的合法性时，监督投票是什么感觉。

sentences.en: Monday, October 24th.
sentences.zh: 10月24日，星期一。

sentences.en: Okay, so Stephen, thank you for making time for us.
sentences.zh: 好的，斯蒂芬，谢谢你抽出时间接受我们的采访。

sentences.en: I know that you're in the thick of it because early voting has actually started in Arizona, so every minute of time we take from you is precious, so we're grateful.
sentences.zh: 我知道你正处于风口浪尖，因为亚利桑那州的提前投票已经开始了，所以我们占用的每一分钟时间都很宝贵，我们对此深表感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciate the opportunity very much, so.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢这次机会。

sentences.en: Stephen Richer oversees elections in Maricopa County, which accounts for more than half of the voters in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 斯蒂芬·里彻负责监督马里科帕县的选举，该县占亚利桑那州选民的一半以上。

sentences.en: And it's the fastest growing county in the United States for, I think, like four out of the last five years, and it is...
sentences.zh: 而且它是美国增长最快的县，我想在过去五年里有四年是这样，它是……

sentences.en: He's a lifelong Republican.
sentences.zh: 他是一位终身共和党人。

sentences.en: ...conservative, movement conservative, Milton Friedman, Federalist Society kid, et cetera, et cetera.
sentences.zh: ……保守派，运动型保守派，米尔顿·弗里德曼、联邦党人学会的拥趸，等等，等等。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, a true believer.
sentences.zh: 所以，是一个真正的信徒。

sentences.en: A true believer.
sentences.zh: 一个真正的信徒。

sentences.en: And in 2018, after a career in business and law, he decided to run for the local office of County Recorder.
sentences.zh: 2018年，在从事商业和法律工作后，他决定竞选当地的县记录官一职。

sentences.en: I thought it was an office that was exciting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一个令人兴奋的职位。

sentences.en: I thought it was an office where you're serving 4.5 million customers.
sentences.zh: 我觉得那是一个服务450万客户的职位。

sentences.en: That's how many people are in the Maricopa County, in Maricopa County, and running a business that happens to be involved in politics.
sentences.zh: 马里科帕县有这么多人口，经营一家恰好涉及政治的业务。

sentences.en: So, you run.
sentences.zh: 所以，你参选了。

sentences.en: It is 2020.
I'm curious, when did you begin to understand just how unusual that particular election was going to be?
sentences.zh: 我很好奇，你是什么时候开始意识到那次选举会是多么不同寻常的？

sentences.en: Was there a specific moment?
sentences.zh: 有没有一个特定的时刻？

sentences.en: And can you set the scene for us a little bit?
sentences.zh: 你能为我们还原一下当时的场景吗？

sentences.en: On election day, I got to a voting location at 6 a.m., and I spent the entire day with my parents, going around to different voting locations,
sentences.zh: 选举日那天，我早上6点到达投票点，我和父母花了一整天时间走访不同的投票点，

sentences.en: speaking to people in line, handing out granola bars to try and garner some favor, introducing myself.
sentences.zh: 与排队的人交谈，分发燕麦棒以试图博取好感，并进行自我介绍。

sentences.en: You know, many people were not familiar with who I was, you know, the position.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人并不熟悉我是谁，也不了解这个职位。

sentences.en: And so, I finished at 7 p.m.
sentences.zh: 所以，我在晚上7点结束了工作，

sentences.en: when that was the last time to get in line for voting locations, and probably got back to my home around 7.45, showered real quickly.
sentences.zh: 那是进入投票点排队的最后时间，我大概7点45分回到家，快速洗了个澡。

sentences.en: It had been a long day, and then I logged on to see the first results at 8 p.m.,
sentences.zh: 那是非常漫长的一天，然后我在晚上8点登录查看初步结果，

sentences.en: and they were not very favorable, to say the leaSt.
sentences.zh: 说得委婉一点，结果并不乐观。

sentences.en: With the first results, I was down significantly.
sentences.zh: 初步结果显示，我落后了很多。

sentences.en: I think it was something like 85,000, 90,000 ballots disadvantaged.
sentences.zh: 我想大概有85,000到90,000张选票的差距。

sentences.en: And it was a blue wave in Maricopa County.
sentences.zh: 马里科帕县出现了蓝色浪潮。

sentences.en: And we thought there was a chance that Republicans would come back, but we didn't know to what extent.
sentences.zh: 我们当时认为共和党人还有机会反超，但不知道程度如何。

sentences.en: And so, my victory party died pretty quickly, and I even tried to go to bed.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的胜选派对很快就结束了，我甚至试着去睡觉。

sentences.en: That was impossible, though.
sentences.zh: 但那是不可能的。

sentences.en: And welcome back to the news at 8 o'clock.
sentences.zh: 欢迎回到8点新闻。

sentences.en: We are staying on top of breaking news just outside of the Maricopa County Recorder's office.
sentences.zh: 我们正在密切关注马里科帕县记录官办公室外发生的突发新闻。

sentences.en: Well, then I started noticing that there were people down at the tabulation center who were protesting, who were chanting, who were disrupting the process.
sentences.zh: 嗯，然后我开始注意到制表中心外有人在抗议、在呼喊、在扰乱工作流程。

sentences.en: That's unprecedented here in Maricopa County.
sentences.zh: 这在马里科帕县是前所未有的。

sentences.en: We'd never had people outside the tabulation center.
sentences.zh: 我们以前从未在制表中心外有过抗议人群。

sentences.en: I think that people had previously viewed it as a mundane but necessary administrative post, and it just had to keep on churning along,
sentences.zh: 我认为人们以前把它看作是一个平凡但必要的行政岗位，它只需要不断运转，

sentences.en: and that there was an understanding that this would be done, and it would take longer than everyone would ideally like in their perfect world,
sentences.zh: 人们理解这项工作必须完成，虽然这比每个人理想中希望的要慢，

sentences.en: in which we would have results instantaneously, but that you didn't go and harass these Republicans, Democrats, Independents, Libertarians of all ages,
sentences.zh: 在那个完美世界里，我们能瞬间得到结果，但你不会去骚扰这些各年龄段的共和党人、民主党人、独立人士和自由意志主义者，

sentences.en: many of whom are senior ages, working together at the tabulation center to tabulate the vote.
sentences.zh: 他们中许多人已是高龄，正在制表中心共同努力统计选票。

sentences.en: It doesn't appear that we'll ever have free and fair elections again.
sentences.zh: 看来我们再也不会有自由公正的选举了。

sentences.en: Why do you say that?
sentences.zh: 你为什么这么说？

sentences.en: Because of the rampant cheating that's happening in Wisconsin, Michigan, and even here in Arizona.
sentences.zh: 因为威斯康星州、密歇根州，甚至就在我们亚利桑那州，猖獗的舞弊正在发生。

sentences.en: And at that point, I became aware that this wasn't going to be like 2018.
sentences.zh: 就在那一刻，我意识到这次选举不会像2018年那样。

sentences.en: This wasn't going to be like 2016.
sentences.zh: 也不会像2016年那样。

sentences.en: So, this is very striking.
sentences.zh: 所以，这非常引人注目。

sentences.en: You are running for the post of overseeing elections in Maricopa County.
sentences.zh: 你正在竞选监督马里科帕县选举的职位。

sentences.en: Certainly, the result of your election is uncertain at this moment, and you're witnessing members of the public, voters,
sentences.zh: 当然，你的选举结果目前尚不确定，而你却目睹了公众、选民，

sentences.en: showing up and essentially harassing the people that you're running for the office of overseeing and working with, right?
sentences.zh: 出现在现场，本质上是在骚扰你竞选监督和共事的人，对吧？

sentences.en: The people in this election office.
sentences.zh: 选举办公室里的那些人。

sentences.en: So, this seems like a complicated moment for you.
sentences.zh: 所以，这对你来说似乎是一个复杂的时刻。

sentences.en: Not terribly.
sentences.zh: 并不完全是。

sentences.en: I thought it was preposterous.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这太荒谬了。

sentences.en: Alex Jones was out there in the parking lot, and it immediately took on a militant vibe with people with weapons there.
sentences.zh: 亚历克斯·琼斯当时就在停车场，那里立刻呈现出一种好战的氛围，有人带着武器。

sentences.en: We are standing in defense of the republic now at this incredible moment.
sentences.zh: 在这个不可思议的时刻，我们正站在捍卫共和国的立场上。

sentences.en: People in military-esque garb in the parking lot saying, stop the count, stop the count, which was befuddling to me because with each successive release of results,
sentences.zh: 停车场里穿着类似军装的人喊着“停止计票，停止计票”，这让我感到困惑，因为随着每一轮结果的发布，

sentences.en: everyone on the republican slate was getting closer and closer to catching their democratic proponent, including, most noteworthily, President Trump.
sentences.zh: 共和党候选人名单上的每个人都越来越接近赶上他们的民主党对手，其中最值得注意的是特朗普总统。

sentences.en: You don't like America, leave it!
sentences.zh: 你不喜欢美国，就离开它！

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Leave it if you don't love it!
sentences.zh: 如果你不爱它，就离开它！

sentences.en: Exactly!
sentences.zh: 完全正确！

sentences.en: It was doing nobody a service,
sentences.zh: 这帮不到任何人，

sentences.en: and for that reason, I posted to social media a number of times that this is not helpful, that they should leave.
sentences.zh: 正因如此，我在社交媒体上多次发帖说这没有帮助，他们应该离开。

sentences.en: What exactly did you say?
sentences.zh: 你具体说了什么？

sentences.en: Because it's interesting, you're talking about voters you assume are republican,
sentences.zh: 因为这很有趣，你谈论的是你认为的共和党选民，

sentences.en: and you're taking to social media, maybe it's Twitter, and saying to them, desiSt.
sentences.zh: 你正在使用社交媒体，可能是推特，对他们说，停止吧。

sentences.en: What specifically are you telling them?
sentences.zh: 你具体在告诉他们什么？

sentences.en: I forget what the exact language was, but basically, guys cut it off.
sentences.zh: 我忘了确切的措辞是什么，但基本上是说，伙计们，停下来吧。

sentences.en: This isn't helping anyone, and we want them to count the votes.
sentences.zh: 这帮不到任何人，我们希望他们统计选票。

sentences.en: The chant should have been, count the votes, thank you, thank you, keep on going, let us know if we can get you donuts or coffee.
sentences.zh: 口号应该是：统计选票，谢谢，谢谢，继续努力，让我们知道是否可以给你们买甜甜圈或咖啡。

sentences.en: Did any of that surprise you, knowing what you knew up to that point about how Donald Trump had primed voters to be thinking about this election?
sentences.zh: 考虑到你当时对唐纳德·特朗普如何引导选民看待这次选举的了解，这一切让你感到惊讶吗？

sentences.en: To actually see it physically showing up outside the office that you're seeking to hold?
sentences.zh: 亲眼看到它出现在你试图担任的办公室外？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, the immediate sensationalization of it, the immediate jumping to a conclusion that things had gone wrong,
sentences.zh: 你知道，那种即时的煽动性，那种立刻跳到事情出了问题的结论，

sentences.en: the fact that somebody like Alex Jones would be welcomed in immediately and embraced in part of the fold was surprising and disturbing to me.
sentences.zh: 像亚历克斯·琼斯这样的人会立刻受到欢迎并被纳入其中，这让我感到惊讶和不安。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So, eventually, of course, the votes keep getting counted.
sentences.zh: 所以，最终，当然，选票还在继续统计。

sentences.en: And you win that office.
sentences.zh: 而你赢得了那个职位。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so, once you win, but knowing what you have seen outside the election office, are you starting to get a little bit nervous about what it's going to mean to occupy this office
sentences.zh: 那么，一旦你获胜，但考虑到你在选举办公室外所看到的一切，你是否开始对担任这个职位意味着什么感到有点紧张？

sentences.en: that you have just won?
sentences.zh: 你刚刚赢得了这个职位。

sentences.en: Well, more immediately, it disrupted my beautiful plans for my post-successful election weeks.
sentences.zh: 嗯，更直接的是，它打乱了我对胜选后几周的美好计划。

sentences.en: What do you mean?
sentences.zh: 你是什么意思？

sentences.en: Well, I planned on rehabilitating the shambles of my professional career just because I had put so
sentences.zh: 嗯，我计划修复我职业生涯的烂摊子，因为我把太多事情搁置了，

sentences.en: much on the back burner in terms of my health, my life, my law practice, talking to family members.
sentences.zh: 包括我的健康、我的生活、我的律师事务所，以及与家人的交流。

sentences.en: I planned on taking a vacation for the first time in over two years, but immediately I got thrown into this morass of misinformation
sentences.zh: 我计划两年来第一次去度假，但立刻就被卷入了这场错误信息的泥潭，

sentences.en: and trying to distill what was fact from what was fiction.
sentences.zh: 试图分辨什么是事实，什么是虚构。

sentences.en: And I was already seen by so many of the people who were engaging with this as the potential answer to these questions.
sentences.zh: 而且，许多参与其中的人已经把我视为这些问题的潜在答案。

sentences.en: And, you know, I was grappling with all of this for the first time as well.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我当时也是第一次应对所有这些问题。

sentences.en: I didn't know what fractional voting meant, which was one of the theories that was being bandied about.
sentences.zh: 我不知道“分数投票”是什么意思，这是当时流传的理论之一。

sentences.en: I was watching all these crazy YouTube videos and researching all these theories.
sentences.zh: 我当时在看所有这些疯狂的 YouTube 视频，研究所有这些理论。

sentences.en: And it was not the romanticized post-election vision that I had yearned for.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我所向往的那种浪漫的选后愿景。

sentences.en: Tell me about some of these terms that you're starting to throw around.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说你开始提到的这些术语。

sentences.en: For example, I think you said fractional voting.
sentences.zh: 例如，我想你说的是“分数投票”。

sentences.en: What are some of these claims that even though you are just a candidate-elect, you're not yet inaugurated, you suddenly feel you need to start grappling with?
sentences.zh: 即使你只是当选候选人，尚未就职，你突然觉得需要开始应对的这些主张是什么？

sentences.en: Fractional voting, which is a facially preposterous claim, is the idea that each vote is tallied not as one or zero,
sentences.zh: 分数投票，这是一个表面上荒谬的主张，其观点是每张选票的统计不是一或零，

sentences.en: a binary number, such that when President Trump gets a vote, it would go in his column as a one.
sentences.zh: 即二进制数字，这样当特朗普总统获得一张选票时，它会以一的形式计入他的栏目。

sentences.en: Fractional voting suggests that the machine would count it as 1.007 or something like that, such that, the theory goes, it wouldn't immediately trigger any sort of concerns,
sentences.zh: 分数投票暗示机器会将其计为1.007之类的数字，这样一来，理论上讲，它不会立即引发任何担忧，

sentences.en: but that it would incrementally add up.
sentences.zh: 但它会逐渐累积。

sentences.en: It's a little bit like the old movie Office Space, where they're basically rounding off the pennies into an account.
sentences.zh: 这有点像老电影《办公空间》，他们基本上把零头四舍五入到一个账户里。

sentences.en: Creates a fortune for the office workers, right?
sentences.zh: 为办公室职员创造了一笔财富，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly, except for I think they got a decimal wrong in that movie.
sentences.zh: 没错，只是我觉得那部电影里他们搞错了小数点。

sentences.en: So this is a conspiracy theory that nefarious forces have tinkered with voting machines in such a way that presumably Republican votes would be counted as less than one full vote.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个阴谋论，认为邪恶势力篡改了投票机，以至于共和党的选票会被计为少于一整票。

sentences.en: Yes, you have the gist of it, but it seems like it's straight out of a Robert Ludlum novel.
sentences.zh: 是的，你抓住了要点，但这看起来就像直接出自罗伯特·勒德拉姆的小说。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: What other theories are you confronting in this period just after you win?
sentences.zh: 在你获胜后的这段时间里，你还面临哪些其他理论？

sentences.en: Switching votes, that the tabulation machines would read it as a Trump vote, but would align it in the Biden column, that Sharpies were causing overvotes,
sentences.zh: 转换选票，即制表机将其读取为特朗普的选票，但将其对齐到拜登的栏目中；或者记号笔导致了多选；

sentences.en: or that they weren't causing votes to be tabulated accurately, that the tabulation equipment was connected to the Internet and therefore susceptible to outside manipulation,
sentences.zh: 或者它们没有导致选票被准确统计；或者制表设备连接到了互联网，因此容易受到外部操纵；
